about.lead: I am an experienced international educator who combines human collaboration, developmental and cognitive psychology, quantum principles and creative processes to foster personalized learning.
about.body: I teach Italian at the Canadian School of Milan and lead workshops for teachers and students across Europe, from Basel and Turin to Rome and Reykjavík. My work moves between divergent and convergent attention, between talking and building, so that ideas become something people can hold.

vision.lead: Learning is not a straight line from not-knowing to knowing. It loops, branches and changes shape with the people in the room. These four principles guide how I design every session.

cards.title: Attention is a catalyst
cards.text: Where attention goes, learning follows. Moving deliberately between divergent and convergent attention turns scattered ideas into insight, and insight into action.

cards.title: Learning is energy exchange
cards.text: Every classroom is a field of human energy. When people listen, respond and build on each other, that energy compounds into something no one could reach alone.

cards.title: Language builds worlds
cards.text: The words we choose shape what we can imagine. Dialogue, across languages, gestures and cultures, is how abstract ideas become shared, tangible worlds.

cards.title: Minds grow when they play
cards.text: Play lowers the stakes and raises curiosity. Challenge, met playfully, is what reshapes the brain, so I design learning that feels like a game worth taking seriously.
